title: The canonical derived direct-image restriction mate is invertible on the other open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], O,P,W opens with W=O∩P, and i:W→P its inclusion. Fix derived module categories on X,O,P,W in one morphism universe [def-pc-derived-category]. Write rP,rW,rO for canonical exact derived restriction, sP for overlap restriction along i, and eP:rP⋆sP≅rW for its canonical composition comparison [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. Let JP=RjP_* and JW=RjW_* be the fixed derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let adjP:rP⊣JP and adjW:rW⊣JW be any adjunctions on these functors. For every B in D(O_P), the morphism rO.map(adjW.homEquiv(JP B,sP B)(eP.inv at JP B followed by sP.map(adjP.counit at B))) is an isomorphism. No covering hypothesis or overlap gluing isomorphism is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] to the inclusions of P and W into X and the open O. Since W=O∩P, both restricted derived direct images identify with the derived direct image to O of B restricted to W. These identifications are valid on unbounded derived categories and natural in B.

proof.text: Check the canonical mate, rather than just existence of an isomorphism. For the canonical derived open adjunctions, represent B by a K-injective complex I on P; its restriction to W remains K-injective by the restriction result used in [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. The comparisons of [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] identify iterated restriction with restriction to W. The displayed mate is induced by the restriction of the P counit, so on an open T of O it is the identity on I(T∩P). This follows from the underived restriction counit and triangle identity, and the derived adjunction construction preserves that identity. Thus the mate is an isomorphism on O. For arbitrary adjP and adjW, uniqueness of adjunctions on fixed left and right functors expresses their units and counits through natural automorphisms of the right adjoints; the new mate is conjugate to the canonical mate by these automorphisms, so remains invertible. Empty opens and empty intersection have zero complexes and require no exception.

theorem derived_open_intersection_mate_isIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (O P W : X.Opens) (hW : W = O ⊓ P) (i : W ⟶ P)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings O.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings P.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (adjP : (schemeOpenRestriction X P).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ schemeDerivedDirectImage P.ι)
    (adjW : (schemeOpenRestriction X W).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ schemeDerivedDirectImage W.ι)
    (B : schemeDerivedCategory P.toScheme) :
    let sP := (schemeOpenOverlapRestriction X i).mapDerivedCategory;
    let eP := schemeDerivedOpenRestrictionCompIso X i;
    IsIso ((schemeOpenRestriction X O).mapDerivedCategory.map
      ((adjW.homEquiv ((schemeDerivedDirectImage P.ι).obj B) (sP.obj B))
        (eP.inv.app _ ≫ sP.map (adjP.counit.app B))))
